q: What prevalence/incidence range does the chapter give for delirium in older ED patients?
explanation:
The chapter reports 6–38% of ED adults older than 65 presenting with or developing delirium (p209).

A. 36–50%: This is the one-year composite frequency of recurrent fall, ED revisit, or death after an initial fall (p213).
D. 80–90%: This is the frequency of PLMS among patients with RLS, not ED delirium (p651; p209).
B. 45–65%: This is the frequency of PLMS among patients with narcolepsy, not ED delirium (p651; p209).

q: Why might caregiver AD8 help when a highly educated patient passes brief performance testing?
o: It obtains a care-partner history of cognitive change from baseline
It measures the patient’s orientation using AMT4
It uses the patient’s performance on O3DY
It establishes a definitive diagnosis of dementia
explanation:
The cAD8 avoids education-related performance-test false negatives by obtaining an informant history of change from baseline (p213).

B. It measures the patient’s orientation using AMT4: AMT4 is a patient performance screen that can yield false negatives in highly educated people (p213).
C. It uses the patient’s performance on O3DY: O3DY is also among the performance screens with this education-related limitation (p213).
D. It establishes a definitive diagnosis of dementia: The chapter explicitly says these brief screening tools are not diagnostic for dementia (p213).

q: What follows uncertain confidence in a patient's ability to report abuse?
o: Record suspicion solely from the cognitive-screen result
Record no suspicion without further assessment
A physical assessment for findings suggesting abuse or neglect
Return to the initial cognitive assessment as the next step
explanation:
Figure 15-4 directs the not-confident reporting-ability branch to physical assessment, integrated with all available information (p214).

B. Record no suspicion without further assessment: No suspicion is a possible downstream judgment after considering available information; it is not the not-confident branch (p214).
A. Record suspicion solely from the cognitive-screen result: AMT4 precedes abuse questions and judgment; the not-confident branch leads to physical assessment, not an automatic suspicion conclusion (p214).
D. Return to the initial cognitive assessment as the next step: The initial cognitive assessment occurs before the abuse questions; the next step on the not-confident branch is physical assessment (p214).
